newsitem.title: USA: Washington court dismisses Medicaid tobacco claims.
newsitem.headline: Washington court dismisses Medicaid tobacco claims.

text.p: A Washington state Superior Court judge dismissed most of the state's claims against cigarette makers in its lawsuit seeking reimbursement for the public costs of treating illnesses related to smoking, two tobacco companies said Tuesday.
A spokeswoman for one of the companies, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, said the remaining claims pertained to antitrust matters and a state law about targetting cigarette marketing to minors.

In an 18-page opinion dated June 6, 1997, Judge George Finkle rejected the state's claims of breach of special and general duties, unjust enrichment, performance of another's duties to the public, and restitution and/or disgorgement of the defendants' profits, the companies said.
Philip Morris Cos Inc, one of the companies that issued a statement about the ruling, maintains that the state's few remaining claims are legally flawed.
Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, said the state was unable to bring claims that satisfied the law regarding a third party bringing claims for damages.
Representatives of Washington's attorney general were not immediately available for comment.
